title: Prepared PDF design
intro: Design for the agreed preparation stage. Dark Start here nodes mark each graph's reading entry; numbered edges indicate ordering. These are workflow graphs, not a formal state model. Geometry and OCR remain later decisions.

groups.title: Assembly and handoff
groups.description: Explicit roles and page selections determine one ordinary prepared PDF.

groups.title: Originals and output publication
groups.description: A complete output becomes visible only at the no-clobber commit point.

discussion.title: Whole-page preservation and safe publication
discussion.summary: Choose a small Python/pikepdf command: front → content → back, whole-page copying, embedded role hints, and no overwrite. The dependency experiment checks copying; implementation still must verify the public command and failure contract.

updatedDiagrams.summary: Defined role grouping, full-page copying and the sole-PDF successor handoff.
Defined validation, private writing and an atomic no-clobber publication point.

diagrams.title: Explicit roles become one prepared PDF
diagrams.caption: Design decision: selections retain argument order within roles, then front precedes content and back follows. Interior cover pages are selected as content. No filename, page count, blank detector or spread classifier determines selection. The processor receives one PDF, and optional embedded roles provide no geometry exemption.

diagrams.title: Publish a complete PDF without overwriting
diagrams.caption: Design decision: dry-run returns after validation without writing. Any pre-commit failure leaves the destination absent or its prior occupant unchanged. A successful link is the commit point; cancellation after it may leave a complete valid output. SIGKILL can leave a private temporary file. Filesystems that cannot perform no-clobber publication fail explicitly. Sources are read-only throughout.
